summary: Iteration 3 (65-tool catalog / 31 categories / everyday tier / dark logo) fully verified. 60/60 backend pytest cases pass (30 iter-1 + 17 iter-2 + 13 iter-3). All expanded-catalog integrity checks pass: 65 tools, 31 categories with NO empty category, every tool (incl. freightpilot, mealmate, giftgenie, threatlens) has non-empty tier / speed / quality_tier / why. Everyday category returns exactly 8 tools ($9-$29). Stripe checkout succeeds for new products (tool_giftgenie, tool_threatlens, tool_freightpilot) — prices synced. MealMate AI demo generates real output. Frontend: Home renders logo-full.png, 65+/30+ hero stats, 'Everyday AI' section with view-all + 8 everyday cards; Marketplace shows 32 filter chips (all + 31 cats), Everyday filter -> 8 tools, Cybersecurity -> 2, Logistics -> 3, tier badges visible; Tool detail for freightpilot & giftgenie shows Tier/Speed/Quality why-panel + reviews section + live simulation; regression: 4 bundles still render, admin dashboard still loads.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py remains at ~646 lines and catalog.py has grown to 561 lines with a mixed responsibility (data + enrichment loop + reviews seed). Recommend splitting server.py into routers/ (already flagged in iter-2) and moving TIER_META + _auto_meta into a small enrichment module — the top-level `for _t in CATALOG:` mutation at import time is easy to miss and re-runs on every reload.
GET /api/tools/{slug}/reviews still does NOT 404 on unknown slug (returns empty array). Kept from iter-2; noting again for consistency with POST behavior.
seed_reviews() is still one-shot (only seeds when reviews collection is empty). If SAMPLE_REVIEWS is edited, reseed requires manual truncate.
CORS still uses allow_origin_regex='.*' with allow_credentials=True — long-standing hardening item from iter-1.

_auto_meta() bases tier purely on price. Most of the 47 new tools' 'why' text is auto-generated from tagline+tier+category — reads fine but is templated; hand-crafted TIER_META entries for high-visibility new tools (freightpilot, threatlens, mealmate, giftgenie, fitforge) would be a small quality lift.

In list_categories(), counts are computed by iterating db.tools rather than $group aggregation — fine at 65 rows, but at N=1000+ this should switch to `db.tools.aggregate([{'$group': {'_id': '$category', 'n': {'$sum': 1}}}])`.
